card.title: OX AND BUCKS
card.text: Deployment: Deal 2 damage to an enemy unit.
card.flavorText: The Oxfordshire and Buckinghamshire Light Infantry, known as the Ox and Bucks, was a British Army regiment which was active from 1881 to 1958. At the start of WWII the 1st and 4th Battalions of the Ox Bucks were part of the British Expeditionary Force and they saw action during the Battle of France. The 1st Ox and Bucks was eventually evacuated from Dunkirk but the 4th Ox and Bucks surrendered in Belgium after being encircled by the German forces. Members of the 2nd Ox and Bucks participated in the Normandy landings and were the first British troops to land on D-Day on June 6th 1944. As part of the 6th Airborne Division they were dropped by Horsa Glider to secure road bridges across the river Orne and the Caen Canal. During this operation they captured the Pegasus Bridge, an operation that was immortalized in the film “The Longest Day”. Later that year, the 1st Battalion took part in Operation Market Garden. The 2nd Battalion was again dropped by glider during the Rhine Crossings in 1945. The regiment's Territorial battalions fought in North Africa, Italy and the Far East. Two companies from the battalion joined the T-Force, a British-American unit sent to capture German scientists and to secure research and industrial technologies late in the war.
